search_row.title: Reaction-diffusion of morphogens accounts for biological pattern
search_row.statement: Chemical substances that react and diffuse through tissue (morphogens) are sufficient to account for the main phenomena of morphogenesis.
search_row.math: no canonical formalization: the claim asserts that a biological pattern is generated by a system of the form u_t = F(u) + D\nabla^2 u with D not proportional to the identity

fields.dct:source: Alan Turing (1952) The chemical basis of morphogenesis
fields.delphi:proposedTest: In a candidate system, identify the interacting molecules, measure their kinetics and diffusion, and confirm novel predictions such as stripe insertion during growth or pattern change after a targeted perturbation, while ruling out mechanical alternatives.
fields.delphi:context: Formal status: a framework rather than a mathematical proposition. Kondo and Asai (1995) confirmed the predicted stripe-branching dynamics in Pomacanthus and Castets et al. (1990) produced Turing patterns chemically. Mechanical buckling, prepatterns and cell-cell signalling can produce the same patterns, so a matching pattern alone does not identify the mechanism.
